The test image shows soybean leaves with irregular yellow/chlorotic patches mixed with brown-reddish necrotic areas, somewhat angular in appearance. Key candidates: Bacterial_Blight (angular spots with yellowish-green halos), Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (mosaic mottling), or Downy_mildew.

Let me view a reference image to compare.

The Bacterial_Blight reference shows early-stage small spots with yellow halos. The test image appears to show a more advanced stage — the lesions have coalesced into large irregular brown-necrotic areas surrounded by extensive yellow-green chlorosis, exactly as described: "Lesions may coalesce to form large, irregularly shaped lesions." The pattern is distributed through the mid-upper canopy, no fungal structures are visible, and the overall mosaic of yellow and brown tissue matches advanced Bacterial_Blight well.
